key_insight: T-ARC improves clustering by combining K-means with a topology-aware graph-cut prior built from persistent homology and a distributionally robust stochastic block model.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to make unsupervised clustering more reliable on non-convex, connected, or interleaved data where Euclidean geometry alone is misleading.
method: Uses a K-means data-fidelity term plus a graph-cut penalty to enforce connectivity-consistent assignments.
Builds a latent graph with a stochastic block model and updates its parameter via distributionally robust optimization.
Derives a persistence-based similarity matrix from H0 persistent homology to encode multiscale topological structure.
evidence_signal: The paper reports strong results on synthetic non-convex datasets and competitive, more stable performance on random Fashion-MNIST subsets, with the highest accuracy on curved and interleaved clusters.
watch_item: The method adds topological preprocessing, graph modeling, and block-coordinate optimization, so performance may depend on the quality and computational cost of the persistence-based graph construction.
paper_title: T-ARC: Topology-Aware Randomized Clustering via Distributionally Robust Stochastic Block Models
